sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Horry County, SC?
sections.html:
Deeds, mortgages and plats for Horry County property are recorded at the Horry County Register of Deeds at 1301 Second Avenue in Conway, SC 29526. The county seat is Conway, which sits on the west bank of the Waccamaw River about 14 miles from the Atlantic coast.

The office is open Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:45 PM. Its page notes that the Customer Service and Recording Desk closes early on the last day of the fiscal year, so check before a June 30 trip.

The county page also points to an E-Recording section, a Request for Documents form, escrow accounts, and a Recording Notification Service meant to flag fraudulent filings against your property. You can read the office page at horrycountysc.gov.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Horry County?
sections.html:
Two charges apply to most deeds: the office's recording fee and the state and county deed fee, often called doc stamps. The recording fee is a flat amount per document. Horry County switched from per-page charges to flat fees on August 1, 2019, and the current schedule sits in a price PDF linked from the office page. Ask the office or open the PDF before you close.

The deed fee comes from state law. Under Title 12, Chapter 24 of the South Carolina Code, the rate is $1.85 for each $500 of value, or fractional part of $500. Of that, $1.30 is the state share and $0.55 goes to the county general fund.

As a worked example only: a deed showing $250,000 of value holds 500 units of $500. At $1.85 each, that is $925 in total, $650 state and $275 county. Your actual figure depends on the value the deed reports.

  • Value means what is paid or owed for the property, in money or money's worth.
  • Debt that stays on the property before and after the transfer can be deducted from value.
  • The seller (grantor) is generally liable for the fee, and the buyer (grantee) is secondarily liable.
  • A value affidavit signed by someone tied to the deal goes with the deed.

sections.h2: Which Horry County deeds are exempt from the deed fee?
sections.html:
South Carolina exempts a list of transfers from the deed fee, but the deed still needs an affidavit that states which exemption applies. The list in Section 12-24-40 is long. These are the ones sellers meet most often:

  • Transfers where the property is worth $100 or less.
  • Transfers to a federal, state or local government body, including a school district.
  • A deed that gives a property back to a mortgage holder through foreclosure or a deed in lieu.
  • A corrective or quitclaim deed that only confirms title already held, with no payment.
  • Transfers between family partnerships or family trusts, or to a partner or beneficiary, with no payment.
  • Transfers with no recognized gain or loss under Internal Revenue Code Section 1041.

If your situation does not clearly match one of these, assume the fee applies and ask the register of deeds before you record. The office can tell you what it will accept for recording.

sections.h2: What else can get a Horry County deed rejected?
sections.html:
The Horry County office page names one hard rule: a vacation time-sharing deed must carry a clear notice on its first page and be titled "Vacation Time Sharing Ownership Deed," or the office rejects it. That rule matters for any owner who holds a time-share interest in a county built around tourism.

Other points to confirm before you submit:

  • Names, legal description and tax map number should match the prior recorded deed.
  • The value affidavit or exemption statement is signed.
  • Fees are enclosed in the amount on the current schedule.
  • Mail goes to the P.O. Box, in-person delivery goes to the Second Avenue address.

When in doubt, call (843) 915-5430 before sending an original.

sections.h2: What happens to the property tax bill after a Horry County sale?
sections.html:
Recording the deed moves your name off the county records, but the tax bill follows the owner of record, so the timing of the recording matters. Horry County mails real property tax notices to the owner of record on October 1 of the tax year, and payment is due on or before January 15 of the following year. Penalties start on January 16, February 2 and March 17 for payments postmarked later. A bill that never arrives does not cancel the penalty.

After a sale, the county tells owners to contact the Tax Assessor at (843) 915-5040. That office also handles address changes and the owner-occupied residence classification. The county's assessment guide says a transfer of an existing interest, including a life estate, counts as an assessable transfer and triggers a new appraisal. The 15 percent cap on increases between reappraisals does not apply to the value in the year the transfer is first taxed.

The county's guide says reappraisal runs every fifth year and describes the 2024 cycle. A legal residence is taxed at 4 percent of value and must be applied for before the first penalty date. A buyer who moves in has to file their own application.

sections.h2: What is Horry County like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Horry County is the largest county in South Carolina by land area, at 1,133.31 square miles, and the fourth most populous. Its 2020 census count was 351,029, and the 2025 estimate is 427,551. Growth has come mostly from retirees and second-home owners, and the median age in 2020 was 49.0.

The economy leans on visitors. In late 2023, accommodation and food service was the largest employment sector at 34,736 jobs, followed by retail trade and health care. Large employers listed for April 2024 include Adidas, the City of Myrtle Beach, Coastal Carolina University, Food Lion, Hilton Grand Vacations, Publix and Walmart.

  • Myrtle Beach is the largest community, and Conway is the county seat.
  • Myrtle Beach International Airport serves the area, and Coast RTA runs 15 bus routes.
  • U.S. 17, 501, 378 and 701 are the main roads, with Interstates 73 and 74 still planned.
  • One school system, the Horry County School District, covers the county.

For a seller, that mix means the owner may live elsewhere, and a house passed down in the family may still sit in an older relative's name. Sorting out the recorded chain of title at the register of deeds is often the first step.

sections.h2: How do you sell a Horry County house with title or tax problems?
sections.html:
Start by pulling your recorded deed from the online index and checking that the name on it matches the person who is selling. If an heir inherited the house and no estate paperwork was filed, the title company will usually require it before closing.

Then check the tax account. Taxes still unpaid after the March 17 penalty date stay attached to the account, so ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure before you set a closing date. Cash Home Buyers can look at a Horry County house as it stands, including one with an unrecorded deed, back taxes or a tenant, and explain the steps in writing. We also tell sellers when a different route fits better.

faqs.q: How much does the Horry County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The office uses flat per-document fees that took effect August 1, 2019, listed in a price PDF on its page. The state deed fee is separate: $1.85 per $500 of value.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed fee when selling a house in Horry County?
faqs.a: The seller is generally liable under South Carolina law, and the buyer is secondarily liable. In practice the closing statement shows who pays, so look at your contract and settlement sheet.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed in Horry County by mail?
faqs.a: Yes. The office lists a mailing address of P.O. Box 470, Conway, SC 29528, and a street address of 1301 Second Avenue for in-person delivery. Confirm fees and any requirements by phone first.

faqs.q: Does a foreclosure or deed in lieu deed pay the deed fee?
faqs.a: No. South Carolina exempts a transfer of mortgaged property to the mortgage holder through foreclosure or deed in lieu, though the deed still needs an affidavit giving the reason.

faqs.q: Who do I call about taxes after selling my Horry County house?
faqs.a: Call the Horry County Tax Assessor at (843) 915-5040 about a sold property, and the Treasurer at (843) 428-2126 about a bill. Taxes follow the owner of record, so make sure the deed is recorded.
